editorial:
Imagine stepping back into 1971 to watch a story that felt way ahead of its time. You get to follow the bond between a lesbian woman and a transgender person who doesn't feel like they fit into just one gender category. The whole vibe is very raw and personal, making you feel like a fly on the wall during their most private moments. It is not a polished Hollywood production, but rather a gritty look at identity and love when the world around you does not understand who you are. You will feel the tension and the warmth as these two people try to navigate a confusing world together.

What really makes this work is how the director gets so close to the subjects. The pacing is slow, which might feel a bit long for some, but it lets you really get to know the people on screen. It is a brave piece of filmmaking that does not shy away from the hard parts of life. If you enjoy deep human stories, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by leaning into the meaning of the title. Instead of giving you a neat answer or a happy ending with a bow on it, it leaves the characters in a state of openness. You see that they are okay with not having all the answers about their gender or their future. It ends on a note of acceptance, showing that being unsure is actually a valid way to live your life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves raw human stories and early queer cinema.
